runtime_status: runtime-evidenced on Windows PowerShell 5.1: every MCP server in three live provider configs completed a real initialize -> tools/list exchange, and the three dead command paths found there were repaired and re-verified. Linux/static/artifact gates pass in CI.
notes: v7.9.9: make the bundle's capability claims match what a clean machine can actually do, without regressing 7.9.8's routing architecture. The central question was whether v7.9.8 overclaimed Hermes' keyless web stack. Re-tested from an isolated HERMES_HOME with every provider credential scrubbed: all five keyless ring vendors (exa, parallel, tavily, firecrawl, keenable) served BOTH search and extract with no key, web_search_tool returned real results in 1.9s, and native keyless extract genuinely renders -- 39,437 chars against a plain urllib fetch's 12,535 on a JS-heavy page (3.1x) in 0.4s. So Hermes already has rendered extraction at zero permanent schema cost, and v7.9.8's decision stands. The reviewer's counter-claim was half right and is now documented precisely: Firecrawl's provider does report is_available()=False without credentials, but that is the KEYED path; is_keyless_available() returns True and the free ring is a separate resolution step. Quoting either method alone misleads. An independent adversarial verification reproduced all of it and found a real upstream defect this pack does not patch: Hermes 0.20.4 matches throttling by string, and Tavily's 'hourly_cap_reached' is not in that list, so the ring stops failing over while four vendors still answer (~15% hard failures during a cap window). Documented rather than claimed away. Firecrawl MCP was re-measured tool by tool with credentials scrubbed: exactly 2 of 25 work keyless (scrape, search), 21 answer 'Unauthorized: API key is required', firecrawl_extract is DEPRECATED rather than key-gated, and firecrawl_parse demands a self-hosted FIRECRAWL_API_URL -- so Firecrawl's own documentation that Search, Scrape and Parse are free does not hold for the pinned server. The catalog's old note claimed interact was keyless and extract needed a key; both were wrong. It is generated now by TOOLS/measure_mcp_capability.py into BUNDLED-TOOLS/capability-records/, which separates KEYLESS, NEEDS_KEY, DEPRECATED, RATE_LIMITED and UNVERIFIED -- the throttle bucket exists because Firecrawl's daily-limit message recommends OAuth and a naive classifier files a working keyless tool as needing a key, which is exactly how a correct measurement got contradicted twenty minutes later. -WithExtras no longer registers an optional-key server for a sliver of itself: firecrawl-mcp is not registered without a key -- and being an mcp-npx component, registering IS installing, so nothing is cached either way -- since keyless it is 2 usable tools for ~9,080 tokens on every turn duplicating a native capability, with -RegisterKeylessExtras as the explicit override. The installed-state doctor now reports capability STATES -- what install-state.json actually recorded, registered (and where), keyless tools, credentialled, schema cost, and why something is deliberately not registered -- after a first cut of it reported 'registered: none' for a machine where everything was registered, twice: once from a wrong call signature and once from catalog ids that differ from the registered server names (codebase-memory -> codebase-memory-mcp, github-mcp-server -> github), now declared. Codex's skills budget was measured instead of guessed with codex debug prompt-input: 146 bundle skills render at ~88 visible chars per description and 142 of the 146 are written longer than that, while 60 skills render at ~183 untruncated -- and cutting every description to 60 chars gave no entry more room, so shortening descriptions is NOT the lever and this release deliberately does not rewrite 146 of them. Entry count is the lever; on this machine 70 of 217 entries come from the bundle's own OPTIONAL manual mega-pack that the installer never deploys. Fixed a defect shipped by v7.9.8.5: it widened check_versions.py and test_version_sources for the first four-part version but not TOOLS/Test-Installed-State.ps1, so the installed-state doctor failed the release that shipped it on a correct tree; a contract now asserts every version gate accepts the shipped version. Routing scenario I added for throttle-vs-auth, and the fixtures gained a scorecard that rewards early correct routing rather than eventual success. 146 canonical skills across 5 provider trees; no new always-on MCP and no new skills.
